newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonian protestors demand government steps down.
newsitem.headline: Macedonian protestors demand government steps down.

text.p: Tens of thousands of demonstrators demanded the government's resignation on Thursday over failed pyramid savings schemes in which over 150 million marks ($88.6 million) have been lost and thousands ruined.
The rally at Makedonia square was organised by the largest right wing opposition party VMRO-DPMNE under the slogan "Halt Macedonia's Economic, Social and State Collapse".
Speakers demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski, the dissolution of parliament and the formation of an interim government to prepare for early elections this autumn.
The demonstrators said that if they failed to get a response within three hours they would continue with the rally every day until their demands were met.
The ruling Social Democratic Alliance is dominated by former communists.

"If these authorities stay another year we will meet the same fate (as of our neighbours). We are not staging a coup, we are only asking for early parliamentary elections," VMRO-DPMNE leader Ljupco Georgijevski told the rally.
He was referring to the political and economic instability in neighbouring Albania, Bulgaria and Serbia.
The demonstrators handed over a document detailing their demands to a parliementary official and dispersed for the night, Macedonian televison reported.
Macedonia's fragile economy has been badly hit by the break-up of the Yugoslav federation in 1991 and by sanctions against its northern neighbour Serbia.
To the south, Greece has imposed its own sanctions against Skopje to punish it for refusing to relinquish the name of Macedonia.
Athens says this shows that Macedonia covets its own northern province of the same name.
